config_hash: analysis-only: consumes artifacts/wp2cert_v3 (7f8658cdfc4cac42) per-draw parts plus one registered lever probe; registered before any attribution was computed
evidence_tier: EVIDENCE-TIER DATA, analysis registration. The v2 validation missed its anti-vacuity clause (median looseness 4.1x on dangerous cells). This analysis attributes the slack term by term instead of accepting it.
question: Which term owns the looseness: the audit plug-in's overshoot (a_plugin - realized excess), the localized reliability bound's MEASURED gap component, its CONFIDENCE charge (the z * binomial SE summed over bins and both weightings), the crossing margin b_own_ucb, or the plug-in SE margin? And is any of it structural (a worst-case constant) rather than statistical?

predictions.P-SA1: CalErr_loc owns the slack: on dangerous cells (archived excess >= 0.005), mean CalErr_loc >= 60% of mean slack (bound - excess).
predictions.P-SA2: RISKY, the tightening diagnosis: within CalErr_loc on dangerous cells, the CONFIDENCE charge (z * SE part) owns >= 50%. If instead the measured gap dominates, the audit model is genuinely miscalibrated inside commit regions and tightening requires better audit models, not more data; that verdict would redirect the paper's certificate section.
predictions.P-SA3: The structural answer to the translated-coordinate hypothesis, stated for the record: the v3 bound contains NO worst-case translation constant by construction (it is assembled in the own-rule coordinate, F19; the m_max * kappa_pred alternative was rejected at the Phase 3 freeze, checkpoint 3). The attribution therefore must account for >= 95% of the slack with the four statistical terms alone (a_plugin overshoot, CalErr gap, CalErr confidence, b_own_ucb + z se_a); any unexplained remainder above 5% falsifies the claim that the F19 dividend was fully banked.
predictions.P-SA4: RISKY, the lever test: quadrupling the held-out samples (n_src = n_tgt = 40000) on a 30-cell dangerous subsample reduces the mean bound by >= 0.010 (the confidence charge scales as one over root n_src; if bounds do not shrink, the slack is gap-dominated or structural and P-SA2's falsifier branch holds).

decision_rule: Attribution on the v3 per-draw parts, dangerous cells only, slack = mean bound - archived excess, components averaged over draws. Lever probe: 30 dangerous cells sampled by largest archived excess, 10 draws each at n_src = n_tgt in {10000, 40000}, same seed streams. Verdicts prediction-by-prediction, misses verbatim.

verdicts.run: artifacts/wp2sa_analysis on the v3 per-draw parts; lever probe 30 worst cells x 10 draws x two audit sizes
verdicts.P-SA1: CONFIRMED: CalErr_loc owns 87.4% of the mean slack (+0.0631) on the 219 dangerous cells.
verdicts.P-SA2: CONFIRMED (RISKY): the confidence charge owns 58.9% of CalErr_loc (+0.0325 vs measured gap +0.0227). About half the total slack is a statistical noise floor, about a third is real audit miscalibration inside commit regions; the two tightening levers are, in order, more held-out data and better audit models.
verdicts.P-SA3: CONFIRMED: the four statistical terms account for 100.0% of the slack (a_plugin overshoot +0.0038, b_own +0.0001, z se +0.0040, CalErr as above). No structural remainder exists; the own-coordinate construction left no worst-case translation constant to remove, i.e. the F19 dividend was fully banked at the Phase 3 freeze.
verdicts.P-SA4: CONFIRMED (RISKY): quadrupling the held-out samples cuts the mean bound on the 30 worst cells from +0.1464 to +0.1162, a reduction of 0.0302 against the registered 0.010 floor. The slack is materially purchasable with audit data.
